summary: Connection-pool proxy strips client id header on streaming retry causing duplicate multipart function calls and short-id collisions
description: Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate downstream webhook POSTs and duplicate function/tool executions when using the streaming Python SDK behind their corporate connection pool proxy. The customer uses short base62 id tokens (12 characters) for per-tool idempotency. Observed behavior appears only when a streaming request is retried after a transient network reset from the proxy. Impact: Duplicate side-effects in customer systems (duplicate invoice creation and duplicate file-processing jobs). Customer blocked from using streaming tool-calls safely in production until root cause is addressed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer opens a streaming create call via Python SDK with function calls that include 'X-Redwood-Idempotency' header set to a 12-char base62 token.
2) Payload includes a multipart file attachment (content-type: multipart/form-data) and a tool invocation 'create_record'.
3) Customer's corporate proxy uses connection pooling and rewrites some headers for long-lived connections.
4) During large uploads (>5MB) the proxy resets the client connection once; client SDK retries streaming request per default backoff.
5) Downstream webhook (customer endpoint) receives two POSTs for the same tool call with different idempotency tokens, and both result in created records.
expected_behavior: On a retry, the SDK or gateway should preserve the original client-provided idempotency token (X-Redwood-Idempotency). Downstream webhooks should only see one effective tool invocation when the same idempotency token is used, preventing duplicate side-effects.
actual_behavior: The proxy strips or rewrites the customer-provided X-Redwood-Idempotency header for the retried streaming request. The SDK then generates a new short base62 id for the retry path, resulting in two distinct idempotency tokens and duplicate webhook deliveries. Additionally, because tokens are short (12 chars), we observed at least one collision in customer logs where different requests mapped to the same short token in their datastore, exacerbating duplicates.
logs:
Customer-provided logs (sanitized):

- 2026-03-09T14:12:06Z Proxy reset connection (RST) while chunked upload in progress
- 2026-03-09T14:12:08Z SDK retry initiated new-idempotency=Xk9bZ7aP3qLt
- 2026-03-09T14:12:09Z Webhook POST /hooks/fn returned 200 for id=Xk9bZ7aP3qLt
- 2026-03-09T14:12:11Z Webhook POST /hooks/fn returned 200 for id=Yc1dM2nQ4rSz
- Duplicate create_record processed in customer's DC.
Attached proxy logs show header drop for 14:12:06-14:12:09 window.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Initial triage by Support: Confirmed duplicates in customer logs and matched timestamps to proxy reset events in customer firewall logs.
2026-03-10 - Reproduced in-house behind a local envoy pool by simulating connection reset at 5MB chunk boundary; observed SDK retry path generated new short id when server-side header not echoed.
Hypothesis A: Edge/proxy dropped 'X-Redwood-Idempotency' header on retry when connection reused/pooled, causing the gateway to treat retry as a new request and generate a fresh id.
Hypothesis B: SDK short-id generation (12-char base62) increases collision risk for heavy customers; customer's internal datastore index is not globally namespaced, allowing collisions to surface.

Additional finding: The gateway respects 'x-forwarded-*' but will only trust downstream idempotency headers if they arrive in the initial CONNECT stream; when headers are missing, gateway auto-assigns 'rw-id' and includes in downstream webhook payload.
comments: Leah Martinez (2026-03-10): Customer provided curl + Python snippet and proxy logs. Asked whether Redwood has guidance for header preservation with connection pools.
Arjun Patel (2026-03-11): Reproduced locally with envoy; opened internal investigation ticket INT-33211 to review edge-proxy header persistence logic.

SRE (Maya Kim) (2026-03-12): Found gateway code path that generates rw-generated id when incoming request lacks X-Redwood-Idempotency. Edge proxy config patch candidate prepared to preserve custom headers across retries (PR referenced).
Customer (Frostline Health, Ops) (2026-03-12): Confirmed workaround works in staging when they disable connection pooling; request guidance for permanent mitigation.
Support (2026-03-13): Recommended short-term mitigations and next steps (see resolution).
resolution:
Temporary workaround: Customer disabled connection pooling and configured proxy to forward custom headers for streaming endpoints; this prevented new id generation in retries.
Planned fix: Edge team will land a gateway change to prefer and persist client-provided X-Redwood-Idempotency across streaming reconnects and retries. Patch PR ready (edge-preserve-idempotency-457); rollout scheduled canary 2026-03-17 then full rollout 2026-03-22.
Longer-term: Recommend customers use 20+ char idempotency tokens (RFC-compliant UUID v4 or namespaced UUID) to reduce collision risk; SDKs will be updated to default to 20-char base62 tokens for enterprise tier and include a warning when customers configure tokens shorter than 16 chars.
Follow-up actions: Create a KB article describing proxy settings and recommended idempotency token length. Owner: Arjun Patel. Target close date: 2026-03-23.
follow_up_tasks: 1) INT-33211 - Edge gateway: ensure X-Redwood-Idempotency header preservation on retries (owner: Maya Kim).
2) SDK-1894 - SDKs: increase default idempotency token length to 20 chars for enterprise builds and add validation (owner: SDK team).
3) KB-article: Write 'Streaming behind corporate proxies' guidance and include sample Envoy config (owner: Docs).
